final_recommendation: The room converged on a concrete ratification pathway: Mexico delivers binding enforcement text Friday morning (1% automatic penalty, 30-day trigger, panelist signature final), Congress certifies by noon and votes same week. Mexico's Attorney General provides written legal opinion today confirming signature is constitutionally binding, eliminating Friday verification delays. This breakthrough unlocks ratification if all parties execute on the timeline.
minority_objections: Canada insisted amendment remain bilateral U.S.-Mexico only, warning that reopening the full protocol would put dairy concessions and Chapter 19 back on the table—politically dead in Ottawa
Business lobby initially resisted conditional floor-vote commitment before seeing text, demanding written timeline guarantees upfront
key_conflicts: Congress vs. Mexico on verification mechanics: Congress demanded independent confirmation that panelist signature is binding under Mexican law before committing to floor vote timeline
Labor/Business vs. Congress on timeline certainty: coalition demanded written floor-vote commitment before seeing Friday draft; Congress refused to bind itself to unseen language
Mexico vs. U.S. on sovereignty: Mexico required joint panels with co-presence in inspections to avoid appearance of unilateral U.S. enforcement inside Mexican facilities
key_concessions: Mexico accepted 1% automatic penalty with 30-day trigger and zero discretion to delay or re-litigate findings—major sovereignty concession
Congress agreed to conditional same-week floor vote if Friday draft contains exact enforcement language—accelerated timeline
Mexico agreed to provide Attorney General legal opinion today confirming panelist signature is constitutionally binding—transparency concession
Business lobby accepted enforcement mechanisms (inspections, penalties) conditioned on timeline certainty—shift from opposition to conditional support
Labor union accepted co-presence model for inspections (not unilateral U.S. inspectors) in exchange for automatic penalties
red_lines: Congress: 1% penalty automatic, 30-day clock starts at panelist signature (not internal approval), zero Mexican discretion to re-litigate
Mexico: joint panels with Mexican representation in findings, co-presence in inspections (not unilateral U.S. enforcement)
Canada: amendment must remain bilateral U.S.-Mexico; reopening full protocol to renegotiate dairy/Chapter 19 is non-starter
Labor: automatic enforcement with real penalties or union walks from deal
Business: written timeline certainty (floor vote same week) or coalition collapses
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Implementation risk: no discussion of what happens if first real violation occurs and Mexico's domestic politics pressure government to resist enforcement despite legal commitments
Precedent risk: creating rapid-response labor enforcement mechanism may set template for future trade agreements that other countries resist
Timeline fragility: entire pathway depends on Mexico delivering perfect text Friday morning and Congress certifying by noon—no contingency if either slips

Public narrative risk if certification takes longer than expected Friday: media actor warned ambiguity kills business support, but room didn't plan for communication strategy if legal review extends past noon
downstream_risk_variables: Whether Mexico's Attorney General opinion actually satisfies Congress legal team today (pre-clears standard) or creates new questions
Whether Friday draft language precisely matches the 1%/30-day/zero-discretion standard or contains any ambiguity that triggers re-negotiation
Whether Congress certification process Friday morning stays within the noon deadline or extends into afternoon (killing same-week vote momentum)
Whether media narrative Thursday/Friday frames this as breakthrough or hedge (directly affects business coalition stability and floor vote count)
Whether Canada's ratification can proceed in parallel or waits for U.S. floor vote (affects trilateral momentum)
uncertainty_notes: Room achieved conditional convergence but left critical execution risks unaddressed: (1) Mexico's AG opinion must arrive today and satisfy Congress legal standard—no fallback if it doesn't; (2) Friday draft must contain exact language with zero ambiguity—no process for resolving minor discrepancies without collapsing timeline; (3) Congress certification must complete by noon Friday—no contingency if legal review takes longer; (4) media narrative must frame this as momentum Thursday—but no coordinated communication strategy discussed. The pathway is real but fragile: any single gate failure (AG opinion, draft language, certification timing, media framing) could cascade into ratification collapse.

marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Drove every exchange: 'votes aren't there as written,' 'Democrats walk,' 'votes disappear,' 'politically dead,' 'ratification dies on the floor'—the entire room organized around unlocking stalled ratification
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_pressure: Central driver: room opened with 'enforcement mechanism—inspections, real penalties, triggers that bite' demand, escalated to '1% automatic penalty 30-day trigger zero discretion,' shaped every concession and red line
marker_evidence.business_lobby_support: Genuinely discussed and shifted position (from opposing amendment to conditional support), demanded timeline certainty as condition for member votes, but not the dominant thread—labor enforcement and ratification risk drove more exchanges
marker_evidence.canadian_domestic_acceptability: Repeatedly surfaced as constraint ('dairy concession politically dead,' 'non-starter domestically') and shaped amendment scope (bilateral only), but didn't drive the room's direction—Canada mostly reacted to U.S.-Mexico dynamics
marker_evidence.mexico_labor_sovereignty_risk: Drove Mexico's position throughout: 'sovereignty questions my government can't swallow,' demanded joint panels and co-presence, required AG legal opinion to confirm binding signature—shaped enforcement architecture but shared stage with labor enforcement pressure
marker_evidence.media_public_pressure: Genuinely discussed as forcing mechanism ('headline that holds this together,' 'run uncertainty story and you lose business coalition'), created urgency for plain-English commitments, but didn't dominate—served as amplifier of other pressures rather than independent driver
marker_evidence.agreement_stability: Central organizing principle: room treated amendment as necessary condition for ratification ('package likely needs amendment to pass'), entire pathway premised on enforcement compromise unlocking votes—drove the bilateral amendment strategy and timeline urgency
